//: TypeScript's half of config/workspace-aliases.ts. That module points Vite at
each publishable package's workspace SOURCE; without the matching `paths`
here, `vue-tsc` falls back to node resolution and reads the package's built
`dist/*.d.ts` instead — so the bundler and the type checker disagree about
what the code is. A docs typecheck then fails on anything added to the
library since its last build, naming a prop or method that plainly exists
(#60, #94), and passes again after a rebuild for no visible reason.
Relative paths in an extended config resolve against the file they are
written in, so these are relative to config/.
Extend this from any app that spreads workspaceAliases() into its Vite
config, and keep the two lists in step.
